notes: Account background: product analytics SaaS used by mid-market ecommerce customers. Sensitive PII in user sessions; requires audit logs + KMS.
Team: 2x ML infra, 3x backend, 1 product owner (Maya Chen). Decision committee: CTO (Ben Hale), Head of Product (Maya), Procurement.

Why Redwood: strong production profile, unified hosted -> dedicated path, explicit autoscale/burst controls. Quote from CTO: 'We need predictable costs and a clear ramp; can't gamble on opaque cloud bursts.'
POC data: ~35M tokens/month projected at full roll-out; current POC sim ~4M tokens/month. Expect seasonal spikes up to 2.2x during promotions.
Latency targets: user-facing chat p50 <= 80ms, p95 <= 250ms. Throughput target: sustain 150 qps steady during peak + burst to 350 qps for 10-30 min windows.
Model prefs: prefer optimized open LLMs (quantized) for cost; willing to eval Redwood-verified model profiles. Need fallback to smaller model for degraded mode.
Routing/fallback: require canary rollouts, A/B split by tenant, auto-fallback to lower-cost variant on capacity constraints.
Security: SSO via SAML, monthly audit log delivery, key management via customer's KMS (bring-your-own). Data residency in us-east required.

Procurement asks: 12-month reserved commitment, 3-month ramp period, 25% built-in burst that can be used monthly, overage pricing cap of 1.5x retail rate (customer proposes), and an automatic credit if SLA breached >1 hour once per quarter.
Quote: finance asked for example invoice for 75k ARR commit tier with burst add-on. SE provided cost model for token-unit math and suggested Optimize recommendations to cut unit cost by ~18%.
Open technical questions: method for billing burst consumption, precise definition of 'burst' window, and rollback SLA for model rollouts.
pricing_negotiation_points: Commit level options: 75k ARR (baseline), 125k ARR (preferred discount band), 250k ARR (enterprise tier) - customer leaning to 125k
Burst allowance: Request 25% reserved burst monthly; propose 10% included + additional burst at 1.25x unit price until cap
Overage multiplier: Customer proposes 1.5x. Redwood proposed tiers: 1.25x up to 20% overage, then 1.75x. Customer pushing for single multiplier -> counter needed.
Ramp schedule: 3-month ramp; month1 = 20% commit, month2 = 60%, month3 = 100%. Need contract language for ramp discounts and true-up billing.
SLA credits: Customer asks for credit if p95 latency > 350ms for >30 minutes. Redwood to propose standard SLA with a single-credit cap per incident.
Contract length: 12 months with option to expand capacity quarterly. Prefer evergreen auto-renew with 30-day notice for downgrades.
Professional services: one-time onboarding fee for VPC setup and KMS integration. Customer requested 2 weeks of SE support included in initial price.
summary_of_requirements: Mid-market analytics SaaS needing hosted->dedicated migration for predictability. Primary asks: VPC private control plane, KMS integration, SSO, audit logs, clear committed tiers with transparent burst & overage rules, 3-month ramp, and canary rollouts. Latency p50 target <=80ms and p95 <=250ms; peak sustained throughput 150 qps with short spikes to 350 qps.
final_notes_for_AE: Keep negotiation flexible on overage multiplier but insist on tiered approach to protect Redwood economics. Offer a 125k ARR pilot with 10% included burst and 3-month ramp; include 2 weeks SE time and a dedicated onboarding checklist. Loop legal early for ramp true-up language.
recent_engagement_outcome: Customer verbally committed to preferred 125k ARR band conditional on overage cap and burst definition. Procurement scheduled to issue PO pending legal review (expected by 2026-04).
